data.title: Global Perspectives on AI Ethics Panel #1: Improving oversight, asking the right questions, and cultivating diversity in AI systems
data.description:
Who is artificial intelligence for? How can we apply a cultural, geographical, and temporal lens to AI to better develop and implement these systems? What are some applications for AI in transport and safety? These are some of the questions the first modules of our new free, online course AI Ethics: Global Perspectives seeks to address.

As to enable a deeper conversation and public dialogue on these issues we asked the respective faculty to take part in a live panel discussion on February 24, 2021 from 12-1 PM EST. Among the distinguished panelists:

- Idoia Salazar, President and Co-Founder of OdiselA

- Danya Glabau, Director of Science and Technology studies at the NYU Tandon School of Engineering

- Jerry John Kponyo, Associate Professor of Telecommunication Engineering, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST)

This panel was facilitated by Stefaan Verhulst, Co-Founder and Chief Research and Development Officer of The GovLab and Julia Stoyanovich, Director of the Center for Responsible AI at NYU.

Value Tensions in the Design Engineering of Intelligent Systems
data.short_desc: On June 15th, Professor Rafael Calvo delivered an insightful talk on “Value Tensions in the Design Engineering of Intelligent Systems” as part of the IEAI Speaker Series, which took place at the TUM THINK Tank. During the event, he shared the inspiration behind his chosen topics, tracing it back to his family’s history in countries with autocratic governments during the cold war era. Driven by the belief that all technologies should prioritize well-being, Professor Calvo emphasized the importance of developing models, methods, and empirical evidence for designing technologies that enhance well-being. He highlighted the need for design engineers to integrate various engineering, design, and innovation approaches.

data.title: Reflections on AI: Q&A with Christoph Bartneck & Dwain Allan
Global Perspectives on AI Ethics Panel #4: data equity, perspectives from the Global South, high risk profiling systems, and the role of universities
data.description:
Data and AI-based technologies are increasingly being leveraged to solve the world’s biggest challenges. However, the rapid adoption of new technology, without attention to the wider social, economic, and political context, can pose unique risks to privacy and security, and threaten to exacerbate social and economic inequalities. It may also perpetuate habits, approaches, and norms that will later prove difficult to reverse.

AI Ethics: Global Perspectives, jointly launched by The Governance Lab (The GovLab) at the NYU Tandon School of Engineering, The Global AI Ethics Consortium (GAIEC), Center for Responsible AI @ NYU (R/AI), and the TUM Institute for Ethics in Artificial Intelligence (IEAI) was designed to increase literacy, awareness and education on the ethical implications of data and AI. We brought together 21 leading global experts in the field of ethical AI to help create a more nuanced understanding of the role data and AI should play in our society.

We release new modules every month, and also host a series of monthly panel discussions with course faculty to enable a deeper conversation and public dialogue on the issues surfaced in each month’s modules. On Tuesday May 11th at 8-9 AM EST the following faculty will join us for the fourth installment of Global Perspectives on AI Ethics:

• Celina Bottino, Project Director at Institute for Technology & Society of Rio de Janeiro (ITS Rio)

• Fabro Steibel, Executive Director at ITS Rio

• Yves Poullet, Co-Chairman of the Namur Digital Institute (NADI) and Eméritus Professor at University of Namur

• Julia Stoyanovich, Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at Tandon School of Engineering, Assistant Professor of Data Science at Center for Data Science, at Director at Center for Responsible AI, New York University

The panel will be moderated by course leads, Christoph Lütge, Director of the TUM Institute for Ethics in Artificial Intelligence (IEAI), and Stefaan Verhulst, Co-Founder and Chief Research and Development Officer at The Governance Lab.
data.short_desc: Global Perspectives on AI Ethics is hosted as a part of AI Week 2021, the nation's only week-long tech festival dedicated to artificial intelligence and its power to revolutionize the world around us.
